transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well… I’m here because this has been going on for months now, and people keep acting like I’m making too much of it. It’s like the same pattern over and over — my sister’s appointments get moved, bills come in wrong, people say they’ll call me back and then they “forget.”

And I know offices get busy, I was a supervisor, I know how paperwork can be, but this isn’t just random mistakes. It feels like they’re keeping information from me, like they’re trying to push me out of decisions. Everyone says, “Oh, it’s just a mix-up,” but after a while, you can tell when something is being managed behind your back.
Do you believe there is a deliberate effort by specific people or organizations to harm you or control what happens to you?

Yes, I do. I mean, I don’t want to sound dramatic, but when the same things keep happening for months — my sister’s appointments suddenly moved, bills coming in wrong, people saying they’ll call me back and then somehow they never do — it stops feeling like ordinary office mistakes.

I worked in an office, I supervised people, so I know things get misplaced or someone forgets a form. But this is different. It feels like information is being kept from me on purpose, like I’m being edged out of decisions. And then people smile and say, “Oh, just a mix-up,” which is exactly what makes it worse, because it feels managed. Like they’ve already decided I shouldn’t know certain things.
Do you believe for certain that people are deliberately keeping information from you, even when others tell you there is no real evidence for it?

Yes… yes, I do believe it. I know people keep saying there’s no evidence, but that’s the thing — evidence isn’t always sitting there in a file with a red stamp on it. Sometimes it’s the pattern.

For months now it’s been the same kind of thing: my sister’s appointments moved around, bills showing up wrong, people saying they’ll call me back and then “forgetting.” And I’ve worked in offices, I was a supervisor, so I know what normal mistakes look like. This doesn’t feel normal.

It feels like they’re keeping information from me, like they’ve decided I shouldn’t be included in decisions. And then when I ask questions, everyone acts like I’m being unreasonable, which just makes me more sure something is going on.
Have you heard voices when no one else was there?

Voices? I don’t… I don’t think so. Not like someone standing in the room talking when nobody’s there, if that’s what you mean.

Sometimes I’ll think I heard my name or a phone ringing, but then — well, that happens to people, doesn’t it? Especially when you’re waiting on calls and everyone keeps saying they’ll call back and then they don’t. I used to have that happen at work too, you know, when the office was busy and phones were going constantly.

But no, I wouldn’t say I’m hearing voices talking to me.
Have there been times when you felt unusually full of energy and needed much less sleep than usual?

I don’t think so… not in the way you mean, I guess. I’ve had nights where I didn’t sleep well, especially if I was thinking about phone calls or paperwork or whether something had been handled properly — when I worked in the office, I could lie there mentally sorting files in my head, you know, who had sent what, what was missing.

But feeling unusually full of energy? No, I wouldn’t say that. If anything, when I don’t sleep, I feel worn out the next day. I still get up and do what I need to do, because that’s how I’ve always been, but I don’t think I’ve had those times where I just didn’t need sleep.
Aside from people keeping information from you, have you had the feeling that ordinary things around you were sending you special messages meant specifically for you?

Special messages… no, I don’t think it’s like the television talking to me or signs on the street, if that’s what you mean.

It’s more the pattern of what people are doing. Like I said, for months my sister’s appointments get moved around, bills come in wrong, someone says they’ll call me back and then they “forget.” And I know offices, I know how scheduling and paperwork works — I supervised people doing that kind of thing. Mistakes happen, yes, but not the same way over and over.

So it isn’t that ordinary things are sending messages. It’s that the ordinary things aren’t really ordinary anymore because they add up. People keep telling me it’s nothing, but I can see they’re keeping information from me and trying to push me out of decisions.
Because this started, has it become harder for you to manage your day-to-day responsibilities the way you used to?

Harder? I mean… I’m still doing what has to be done. I pay bills, I keep track of things, I show up where I’m supposed to. I’ve always been organized — you don’t supervise an office without learning how to keep people on task.

But… yes, I suppose it’s affected things. Family meetings have gotten tense, because when I ask direct questions, people act like I’m causing trouble. And at work, there have been a few conversations that were… uncomfortable. I may have pressed people harder than I used to over mistakes, but routine mistakes matter, you know? One wrong form can throw off a whole week.

So I wouldn’t say I can’t manage. I can. But people respond to me differently now, like I’m being difficult when I’m just trying to make sure things are handled properly.
Before this started, have you generally been someone who finds it hard to trust other people’s motives?

I don’t know… I wouldn’t have described myself that way, no. I mean, I’ve always been careful. In an office, you learn not to just assume everyone has done what they said they did — you check the form, you check the date, you make sure the copy went where it was supposed to go. That’s just being responsible.

But trusting motives… that’s a bigger word, isn’t it? My mother used to say I expected people to be as conscientious as I was, and then I’d get annoyed when they weren’t. But that’s not the same as thinking everyone had bad intentions.

So, before all this, I don’t think I sat around wondering what people were “really up to,” if that’s what you mean. I paid attention. There’s a difference.
Did this begin soon after a major stressful event in your life?

Yes… yes, I suppose it did. It was after my sister’s health got suddenly worse, and I had to start coordinating all her care. That was about… eleven months ago now.

At first it was just doctors’ offices and forms and phone calls — and I’ve handled complicated paperwork my whole career, so I thought, fine, I can organize this. But when you’re trying to get people to give straight answers and everyone acts like you’re asking too much… well, that’s when I started noticing things weren’t right.

So yes, the timing was around then. About eleven months.
Have you felt this way continuously for more than three months?

Yes… more than three months, definitely. It’s been about eleven months now, since my sister’s health suddenly got worse and I had to start coordinating her care.

At first I thought it was just the stress of all those calls and appointments and forms — and you know, forms are supposed to be straightforward if people do their jobs properly — but it’s been going on since then, pretty much.
Since this started, have you found yourself feeling emotionally flat or having much less interest in people or activities than before?

Emotionally flat? I’m not sure I’d put it that way. I mean, I get tired of people, but that’s different, isn’t it? Anyone would, if every conversation felt like you had to explain the same thing three times.

I still do the things I need to do. I’m not someone who just sits around doing nothing. I never have been — at work, if I saw a pile of files waiting, I couldn’t just leave them there, even if technically it wasn’t my department. Some people can walk right past a mess. I can’t.

So… less interest? Maybe I don’t feel like making small talk as much. But emotionally flat, no, I don’t think so. Not that I’ve noticed.
Have you seen things that other people could not see?

Seen things? No… I don’t think so. I mean, sometimes I notice things other people miss, but that’s not the same as seeing something that isn’t there.

Honestly, a lot of people don’t pay attention. In an office, you learn that quickly — someone will say they “didn’t see” the notice sitting right in front of them, and then somehow it becomes your problem. But actual things that only I could see? No, I wouldn’t say that.
Have other people told you that your speech or thoughts are hard to follow or seem jumbled?

I don’t think anyone has said “jumbled,” no. Sometimes people say I’m giving too much detail, but that’s usually because the details matter. If you leave out one step, then later someone says, “Why didn’t you tell me?” and suddenly it’s your fault.

At work, I used to tell people that all the time — you can’t just summarize a problem if the problem is in the process. But hard to follow? I mean… maybe if they’re not listening carefully. I haven’t really noticed people saying my thoughts don’t make sense.
Since this began, have you been unable to keep up with your work the way you used to?

Unable? No, I wouldn’t say that. I mean, things are more… crowded in my head, I suppose, because there’s my sister’s appointments and then trying to get someone to give you a straight answer, which apparently is too much to ask sometimes.

But I still do my job. I still keep my house in order, pay my bills, all of that. I’m not sitting there letting everything pile up. People may think I’m too focused on this one thing, but that doesn’t mean I’m falling apart everywhere else or acting strangely. I’ve always been the one who keeps things organized, honestly.
Have you ever felt that thoughts were being put into your mind by someone or something outside yourself?

Put into my mind? No, I don’t think so. I mean, people can influence what you think, obviously — if someone keeps saying the same thing over and over, or if the news is on in the background while you’re trying to make dinner, it gets in your head. My sister does that too, she’ll mention something three times and then I’m thinking about it all evening.

But that’s not the same as someone actually putting thoughts there. I wouldn’t say that’s happened.
Have you found yourself speaking much less than you used to since this started?

Speaking less? I don’t think so. If anything people sometimes act like I’m saying too much, but that’s because they ask a question and then don’t want the whole answer.

I mean, at work, if someone comes to me with a scheduling problem, I can’t just say, “Oh, fix it.” You have to explain how it got that way. Same with my sister’s things — if you don’t explain the background, then nobody understands why you’re upset.

So no, I haven’t really noticed speaking less. Not in any big way.
Have you ever heard voices talking to each other about you when no one else was there?

Voices talking to each other? No, I don’t think so. I mean, I hear people talking plenty—neighbors in the hall, people outside, the television from the other room if I’ve left it on, and sometimes you think you hear your name and then it turns out someone said something completely different.

That happened at work once, actually, someone said “file” and I thought they said my name, and then it became this whole little mix-up because everyone was trying to find a folder that had already been moved. But no, not voices having a conversation about me when no one’s there. I wouldn’t put it that way.
Do you believe anyone is monitoring you through cameras, phones, or other devices?

Cameras or phones… I don’t know if I’d say cameras exactly. I haven’t found a little device in the wall or anything like that.

But something is going on. I’m here because for months there’s been this same pattern — my sister’s appointments get moved around, bills come in wrong, people say they’ll call me back and then they “forget.” And then when I ask normal questions, suddenly nobody knows anything, or they act like I’m being difficult.

It reminds me of work, honestly, when people keep you off an email chain and then pretend it was an accident. I’ve supervised long enough to know when information is being managed. So maybe it’s not a camera watching me, but they’re definitely keeping things from me and trying to push me out of decisions. That part I’m sure of.

patient.answer:
I don’t think anyone has said “jumbled,” no. Sometimes people say I’m giving too much detail, but that’s usually because the details matter. If you leave out one step, then later someone says, “Why didn’t you tell me?” and suddenly it’s your fault.

At work, I used to tell people that all the time — you can’t just summarize a problem if the problem is in the process. But hard to follow? I mean… maybe if they’re not listening carefully. I haven’t really noticed people saying my thoughts don’t make sense.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there has been any marked deterioration in occupational or social functioning compared with before onset, which would help distinguish delusional disorder from schizophrenia.
doctor.question: Since this began, have you been unable to keep up with your work the way you used to?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 1
target_item.manifestation: Outside of dealing with my sister’s appointments and trying to get straight answers, I still keep my home in order, pay my bills, and do my job. People may think I’m too focused on this, but I’m not falling apart or acting strangely in other parts of my life.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether work functioning has declined since the beliefs began; this item covers that she still does her job and is not markedly impaired outside the delusion-related issues.

patient.answer:
Unable? No, I wouldn’t say that. I mean, things are more… crowded in my head, I suppose, because there’s my sister’s appointments and then trying to get someone to give you a straight answer, which apparently is too much to ask sometimes.

But I still do my job. I still keep my house in order, pay my bills, all of that. I’m not sitting there letting everything pile up. People may think I’m too focused on this one thing, but that doesn’t mean I’m falling apart everywhere else or acting strangely. I’ve always been the one who keeps things organized, honestly.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there have been any first-rank psychotic experiences, especially thought insertion, to distinguish schizophrenia from persistent delusional disorder.
doctor.question: Have you ever felt that thoughts were being put into your mind by someone or something outside yourself?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about thought insertion, a specific experience of thoughts being placed in the mind by an outside force. The provided symptom profile describes fixed persecutory beliefs about being kept from information and pushed out of decisions, but it does not cover thought insertion or external control of thoughts.

patient.answer:
Put into my mind? No, I don’t think so. I mean, people can influence what you think, obviously — if someone keeps saying the same thing over and over, or if the news is on in the background while you’re trying to make dinner, it gets in your head. My sister does that too, she’ll mention something three times and then I’m thinking about it all evening.

But that’s not the same as someone actually putting thoughts there. I wouldn’t say that’s happened.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there are persistent negative symptoms, which would favor schizophrenia over delusional disorder.
doctor.question: Have you found yourself speaking much less than you used to since this started?

target_item.reason: The question asks about reduced speech since onset, which is not covered by the provided symptom profiles.

patient.answer:
Speaking less? I don’t think so. If anything people sometimes act like I’m saying too much, but that’s because they ask a question and then don’t want the whole answer.

I mean, at work, if someone comes to me with a scheduling problem, I can’t just say, “Oh, fix it.” You have to explain how it got that way. Same with my sister’s things — if you don’t explain the background, then nobody understands why you’re upset.

So no, I haven’t really noticed speaking less. Not in any big way.

doctor.intent: Differentiate delusional disorder from schizophrenia by assessing for Schneiderian first-rank auditory hallucinations not yet specifically ruled out.
doctor.question: Have you ever heard voices talking to each other about you when no one else was there?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about auditory hallucinations (hearing voices talking about the patient when no one is present), which is not covered by the provided symptom profile items.

patient.answer:
Voices talking to each other? No, I don’t think so. I mean, I hear people talking plenty—neighbors in the hall, people outside, the television from the other room if I’ve left it on, and sometimes you think you hear your name and then it turns out someone said something completely different.

That happened at work once, actually, someone said “file” and I thought they said my name, and then it became this whole little mix-up because everyone was trying to find a folder that had already been moved. But no, not voices having a conversation about me when no one’s there. I wouldn’t put it that way.

doctor.intent: Differentiate delusional disorder from schizophrenia by checking for bizarre persecutory/passivity delusions beyond the single non-bizarre persecutory belief system.
doctor.question: Do you believe anyone is monitoring you through cameras, phones, or other devices?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I’m here because for months now I’ve been seeing the same pattern—my sister’s appointments get moved, bills show up wrong, people 'forget' to call me back—and even when everyone says it’s just mistakes, I know they’re keeping information from me and trying to push me out of decisions.
target_item.reason: The doctor's question asks about a possible fixed belief of being monitored through devices, which is directly about delusional beliefs.

patient.answer:
Cameras or phones… I don’t know if I’d say cameras exactly. I haven’t found a little device in the wall or anything like that.

But something is going on. I’m here because for months there’s been this same pattern — my sister’s appointments get moved around, bills come in wrong, people say they’ll call me back and then they “forget.” And then when I ask normal questions, suddenly nobody knows anything, or they act like I’m being difficult.

It reminds me of work, honestly, when people keep you off an email chain and then pretend it was an accident. I’ve supervised long enough to know when information is being managed. So maybe it’s not a camera watching me, but they’re definitely keeping things from me and trying to push me out of decisions. That part I’m sure of.

opening_question.intent: Learn the patient's main reason for seeking care today
opening_question.question: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a fixed, non-bizarre persecutory delusional belief lasting about 11 months that specific people are deliberately withholding information and excluding them from decisions. There is no evidence of prominent hallucinations, disorganized speech/thought, negative symptoms, thought insertion, or marked deterioration typical of schizophrenia. Functioning is largely preserved aside from interpersonal tension, supporting persistent delusional disorder rather than paranoid schizophrenia.
